paragraphs: More than 300,000 people work for the State in Ireland. They plan to stop work for a second time. The strike will be on Thursday, 12 November.
The Government offered a pay rise of 7.75% over two and a half years. The unions said no. They say the offer is too small. Prices for food and homes are going up fast.
The strike will close schools. Thousands of hospital visits will be cancelled. There will also be a march in Dublin. On the same day, EU leaders will meet in Dublin.
Minister Jack Chambers said the strike is very bad news. Both sides are now talking to a small independent group. They hope it can help them agree.

他們計劃第二次停工。
罷工將在11月12日星期四舉行。
政府提出在兩年半內加薪7.75%。
工會拒絕了。
他們說這個方案太少了。

罷工會讓學校停課。
數千個醫院門診將被取消。
都柏林也會有遊行。
同一天，歐盟領袖將在都柏林開會。
部長傑克·錢伯斯說這次罷工是很糟的消息。
雙方現在都在和一個獨立小組談話。
他們希望這個小組能幫助雙方達成協議。

paragraphs: More than 300,000 public sector workers in Ireland are getting ready for a second strike. It will take place on Thursday, 12 November. Unions say they will also make their work-to-rule action stronger. This means workers only do the exact tasks in their contracts.

The unions rejected a Government pay offer worth 7.75% over 30 months. Most of it, 6.75%, would be paid in several parts. The other 1% would come from local bargaining, which pays for special deals for certain jobs. Unions say they were promised 2% for this.

Kevin Callinan leads the union side in the talks. He said the offer was far below what workers expected. He said the unions had agreed to the Government's wishes on the length of the deal, but the Government did not do enough on the cost of living.

Adrian Kane from the SIPTU union talked about low-paid workers. In the last deal, people earning under €50,000 got a guaranteed minimum rise. This time there is no such promise, and he called this very disappointing.

The strike will close schools and cancel thousands of hospital appointments. There will be a march in Dublin and smaller events around the country. It also falls on the same day as a meeting of EU leaders in Dublin.

Jack Chambers, the Minister for Public Expenditure, said the strike was extremely regrettable. On Tuesday, both sides met separately with a three-person group led by Kevin Foley, the head of the Workplace Relations Commission. They hope this group can help restart the talks.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭超過三十萬名公部門員工正準備第二次罷工。
罷工將在11月12日星期四舉行。
工會說他們也會加強「依規工作」的行動。
這表示員工只做合約裡規定的工作。
工會拒絕了政府提出、30個月內共7.75%的加薪方案。
其中大部分，也就是6.75%，會分幾次發放。
另外1%來自「地方協商」，用來支付某些職位的特別安排。
工會說他們曾被承諾這部分有2%。
凱文·卡利南是談判中工會方的代表。
他說這個方案遠低於員工的期望。
他說工會已經同意政府對協議期限的要求，但政府在生活成本問題上做得不夠。
SIPTU工會的阿德里安·凱恩談到低薪員工。
在上一份協議中，年收入低於五萬歐元的人有保證的最低加薪。
這次沒有這樣的承諾，他說這非常令人失望。
罷工將使學校停課，並取消數千個醫院預約。
都柏林會有遊行，全國各地也有較小型的活動。
罷工也剛好和歐盟領袖在都柏林開會是同一天。
公共支出部長傑克·錢伯斯說這次罷工非常令人遺憾。
週二，雙方分別與由勞資關係委員會主席凱文·佛利領導的三人小組會面。
他們希望這個小組能幫助重新開始談判。

paragraphs: More than 300,000 public sector workers are preparing to walk out for a second time on Thursday, 12 November, after their unions rejected a pay offer worth 7.75% over two and a half years. The unions also plan to step up their existing work-to-rule campaign.

Under the proposal, workers would receive 6.75% in instalments over the 30-month agreement. A further 1% would come from a local bargaining fund, which is used to finance special pay arrangements for particular grades, but it would only be paid near the end of the deal. Unions insist they were promised 2% for local bargaining under the previous agreement.

Chief union negotiator Kevin Callinan said the offer fell well short of expectations. He argued that unions had accepted the Government's preferences on the length of the deal and on productivity, but that ministers had failed to move far enough on the cost of living.

SIPTU's Adrian Kane highlighted the absence of guaranteed minimum increases for workers earning less than €50,000. In the last agreement, those guarantees lifted the lowest-paid workers' rises from a headline figure of 9.25% to just over 17%.

The stoppage is expected to close schools, cancel thousands of hospital appointments and disrupt other services. It will also coincide with a meeting of EU heads of government in Dublin, held as part of Ireland's EU Presidency, and unions are planning a demonstration in the capital.

Public Expenditure Minister Jack Chambers described the escalation as extremely regrettable and said the Government wanted a deal that was fair to workers but also financially sustainable. On Tuesday, both sides held separate meetings with a three-person steering group chaired by Kevin Foley, head of the Workplace Relations Commission, in an effort to break the deadlock.
sentZh: 工會拒絕了兩年半共7.75%的加薪方案後，超過三十萬名公部門員工準備在11月12日星期四第二次罷工。
工會也計劃加強目前進行中的依規工作行動。
根據這項提案，員工將在30個月的協議期間分期獲得6.75%的加薪。
另外1%來自地方協商基金，用於支付特定職級的特別薪資安排，但要到協議快結束時才會發放。
工會堅稱，上一份協議曾承諾地方協商有2%。
工會首席談判代表凱文·卡利南說，這個方案遠遠不如預期。
他認為工會已接受政府對協議期限和生產力的偏好，但部長們在生活成本問題上讓步不夠。
SIPTU的阿德里安·凱恩強調，這次沒有為年收入低於五萬歐元的員工提供保證的最低加薪。
在上一份協議中，這些保證讓最低薪員工的加薪幅度從表面上的9.25%提高到略超過17%。
這次停工預計會讓學校停課、取消數千個醫院預約，並干擾其他服務。
罷工也將與愛爾蘭擔任歐盟輪值主席國期間在都柏林舉行的歐盟領袖會議撞期，工會還計劃在首都示威。
公共支出部長傑克·錢伯斯形容事態升級極為遺憾，並說政府希望達成對員工公平、在財政上也可持續的協議。
週二，雙方分別與勞資關係委員會主席凱文·佛利主持的三人指導小組會面，努力打破僵局。

paragraphs: More than 300,000 public servants are poised to down tools for a second time on Thursday, 12 November, having spurned a pay offer worth 7.75% over 30 months. Their unions have also vowed to intensify the work-to-rule that is already in force.

The package on the table comprises 6.75% paid in staggered instalments, together with a further 1% from a local bargaining pot that funds bespoke arrangements for specific grades. Crucially, that element would only materialise towards the tail end of the deal, and unions maintain that the previous agreement earmarked 2% for this purpose.

Kevin Callinan, who leads the union side, said the offer fell woefully short. In his view, unions had bent over backwards to accommodate the Government's wishes on duration and productivity, only for ministers to stand firm on the cost of living and local bargaining.

SIPTU's Adrian Kane lamented the omission of guaranteed minimum increases for those earning under €50,000. Such guarantees, he noted, had boosted the lowest-paid workers' rises in the last deal from a headline 9.25% to just over 17%.

The walkout threatens to shut schools, scupper thousands of hospital appointments and hamper a raft of other services. Awkwardly for the Government, it also coincides with a gathering of EU leaders in Dublin under Ireland's EU Presidency, while unions intend to stage a demonstration in the capital.

Public Expenditure Minister Jack Chambers branded the escalation extremely regrettable, insisting that any settlement must be both fair to staff and fiscally prudent. In a bid to break the impasse, both camps held separate talks on Tuesday with a three-member steering group chaired by Kevin Foley, head of the Workplace Relations Commission.
sentZh: 超過三十萬名公務員在拒絕30個月共7.75%的加薪方案後，準備於11月12日星期四第二次放下工作罷工。
他們的工會也誓言加強已在實施中的依規工作行動。
目前提出的方案包括分階段發放的6.75%，以及另外來自地方協商基金的1%，用於特定職級的專屬安排。
關鍵在於，這部分要到協議尾聲才會兌現，而工會堅稱上一份協議曾為此指定2%。
代表工會方的凱文·卡利南說，這個方案差得太遠。
他認為工會已竭盡全力配合政府對期限和生產力的要求，部長們卻在生活成本和地方協商上寸步不讓。
SIPTU的阿德里安·凱恩對方案中沒有為年收入低於五萬歐元者提供保證最低加薪表示惋惜。
他指出，這類保證在上一份協議中把最低薪員工的加薪從表面的9.25%拉高到略超過17%。
這次罷工可能讓學校關閉、使數千個醫院預約泡湯，並妨礙許多其他服務。
令政府尷尬的是，罷工也與愛爾蘭擔任歐盟輪值主席國期間在都柏林舉行的歐盟領袖聚會撞期，而工會打算在首都發起示威。
公共支出部長傑克·錢伯斯稱事態升級極為遺憾，並堅持任何協議都必須對員工公平且財政審慎。
為了打破僵局，雙方週二分別與勞資關係委員會主席凱文·佛利主持的三人指導小組會談。

paragraphs: More than 300,000 public sector employees are scheduled to undertake a second strike on Thursday, 12 November, following their unions' rejection of a pay proposal worth 7.75% over a 30-month period. In addition, the unions intend to escalate their existing work-to-rule action.

The proposal consists of 6.75% distributed in phased instalments, supplemented by a further 1% allocated to local bargaining, a mechanism that finances specific arrangements for particular grades. However, this component would not be disbursed until the latter stages of the agreement, and the unions contend that the preceding deal had committed 2% to this purpose.

According to chief union negotiator Kevin Callinan, the offer was substantially below expectations. He maintained that, although the unions had accommodated the Government's priorities regarding duration and productivity, the State had made insufficient concessions on the cost of living.

Adrian Kane of SIPTU emphasised the absence of guaranteed minimum increases for employees earning less than €50,000. Consequently, he argued, the lowest-paid would be disproportionately affected, given that such provisions had previously raised their increases from a nominal 9.25% to slightly over 17%.

The industrial action is anticipated to result in school closures, the cancellation of thousands of hospital appointments and substantial disruption to other services. Moreover, it coincides with a summit of EU leaders in Dublin during Ireland's EU Presidency, and a demonstration is planned in the capital.

Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers characterised the escalation as extremely regrettable, stating that any settlement must be equitable for workers while remaining fiscally sustainable. Nevertheless, in an attempt to resolve the impasse, both parties met separately on Tuesday with a three-member steering group chaired by Kevin Foley, head of the Workplace Relations Commission.

此外，工會打算升級現有的依規工作行動。
該提案包括分階段發放的6.75%，另加撥給地方協商的1%；地方協商是一種為特定職級提供專門安排的機制。
然而，這部分要到協議後期才會發放，而工會主張上一份協議曾為此承諾2%。
根據工會首席談判代表凱文·卡利南的說法，這個方案大幅低於預期。
他堅稱，雖然工會已配合政府在期限和生產力方面的優先考量，但國家在生活成本上的讓步不足。
SIPTU的阿德里安·凱恩強調，方案中沒有為年收入低於五萬歐元的員工提供保證最低加薪。
他認為，因此最低薪者將受到不成比例的影響，因為這類條款過去曾把他們的加薪從名目上的9.25%提高到略超過17%。
這次勞工行動預計將導致學校停課、數千個醫院預約取消，並對其他服務造成重大干擾。
此外，罷工恰逢愛爾蘭擔任歐盟輪值主席國期間在都柏林舉行的歐盟領袖峰會，首都也計劃舉行示威。
公共支出部長傑克·錢伯斯形容事態升級極為遺憾，並表示任何協議都必須對員工公平，同時在財政上可持續。
